title: Ultra-long Read Sequencing for Whole Genomic DNA Analysis
protocol: Make 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) buffer by adding 100 mL of PBS (10x) to 900 mL of water and mixing well.

Prepare lysis buffer by adding 43.5 mL of water, 500 μL of Tris (1 M, pH 8.0), 1 mL of sodium chloride (NaCl) (5 M), 2.5 mL of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) (0.5 M, pH 8.0), and 2.5 mL of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) (10%, wt/vol) to a tube and mixing well.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the medium and resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of 1x PBS buffer.
Centrifuge again at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature, discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of 1x PBS buffer.
If using a frozen cell pellet, wash with 5 mL of 1x PBS buffer.
Centrifuge the solution at 200 x g for 5 min at room temperature, discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 200 μL of 1x PBS buffer.
Prepare 10 mL of lysis buffer in a 50 mL tube.
Add the 200 μL cell suspension to the lysis buffer and vortex at the highest speed for 3 s.
Incubate the solution at 37 °C for 1 h.
Add 2 μL of RNase A (100 mg/mL) to the lysate.
Gently rotate the 50 mL tube to mix the sample.
Incubate the solution at 37 °C for 1 h.
Add 50 μL proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to the lysate.
Gently rotate the 50 mL tube to mix the sample.
Incubate the solution at 50 °C for 2 h, gently mixing every 30 min.
Remove the 50 mL tube from 50 °C and let stand at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 10 mL of the phenol layer of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1, vol/vol/vol) to the lysate and rotate the tube on a rotator mixer at RT in a fume hood at 20 rpm for 10 min.
Centrifuge two 50 mL gel tubes at 1,500 x g for 2 min at RT.
Pour the sample/phenol solution into one of the prepared 50 mL gel tubes and centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 10 min at RT.
Pour the supernatant into a new 50 mL tube.
Add 10 mL of the phenol layer of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1, vol/vol/vol) to the supernatant and rotate on a rotator mixer at RT in a fume hood at 20 rpm for 10 min.
Pour the supernatant into a new 50 mL tube.
Add 25 mL of ice-cold 100% ethanol and gently rotate the tube by hand until DNA precipitates.
Carefully take out the HMW DNA with a bent 20 μL tip and let the liquid drop off.
Place the HMW DNA into a 50 mL tube containing 40 mL of 70% ethanol.
Gently invert the tube 3 times to wash the DNA.
Repeat step to collect DNA from the 70% ethanol tube.
Place the HMW DNA into a 2 mL tube containing 1.8 mL of 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge the washed HMW DNA at 10,000 x g for 3 s at RT.
Pipette to remove residual ethanol without disturbing the DNA pellet.
Incubate the 2 mL tube at 37 °C for 10 min with the lid open.
Add 1 mL of TE (10 mM Tris and 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) to the 2 mL tube if using mechanical shearing method.
Add 200 μL of 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) with 0.02% Triton X-100 to the 2 mL tube if using transposase-based fragmentation method.
Let the tube stand at 4 °C in dark for 48 h to fully resuspend the DNA pellet.
Store HMW DNA at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Thaw FFPE DNA repair buffer on ice.
Vortex FFPE DNA repair buffer and spin down to mix.
Thaw end repair/dA-tailing buffer on ice.
Vortex end repair/dA-tailing buffer and spin down to mix.
Thaw adapter mix (AMX) on ice.
Pipette AMX and spin down to mix.
Thaw adapter bead binding buffer (ABB) on ice.
Pipette ABB and spin down to mix.
Thaw running buffer with fuel mix (RBF) at room temperature.
Vortex RBF and spin down to mix.
Thaw elution buffer (ELB) at room temperature.
Vortex ELB and spin down to mix.
Thaw library loading beads (LLB) at room temperature.
Pipette LLB to mix before use.
Check the quality and quantity of HMW DNA from step 1.21.1.
Pipette out 20 μL of DNA into new 1.5 mL tubes using P200 wide bore tips from three different locations in the HMW DNA tube.
Take 1 μL from each of the three aliquots to detect concentration using a fluorometer and quality using a UV reading.
Check multiple times to confirm results.
Transfer remaining 940 μL of HMW DNA into a 50 mL tube cap with a P1000 wide bore tip.
Aspirate all DNA into a 1 mL syringe without the needle.
Put a 27 G needle onto the syringe and eject all DNA into the cap gently and slowly (~10 s).
Take off the 27 G needle from the syringe.
Repeat steps 2.1.4 and 2.1.5 for 29 times for a total of 30 passes through the needle.
Store sheared HMW DNA at 4°C in the dark for up to 24 hours.
Prepare the DNA repair reaction by adding 100 μL of sheared HMW DNA, 15 μL of FFPE DNA repair buffer, 12 μL of FFPE DNA repair mix, and 16 μL of nuclease-free water in a 0.2 mL tube.
Mix the reaction gently by flicking the tube six times and spin down to remove bubbles.
Incubate the reaction at 20°C for 60 minutes.
Transfer the sample into a new 1.5 mL tube with a P200 wide bore tip.
Resuspend the magnetic beads by pipetting or vortexing.
Add 143 μL of beads (1x) to the DNA repair reaction and mix gently by flicking the tube six times.
Rotate the tube on a rotator mixer at room temperature at 20 rpm for 30 minutes.
Spin down the sample at 1,000 x g for 2 seconds at room temperature.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack for 10 minutes and discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Add 400 μL of freshly prepared 70% ethanol to the pellet while keeping the tube on the magnetic rack.
Remove the 70% ethanol after 30 seconds.
Repeat step 2.1.11 once.
Spin down the sample at 1,000 x g for 2 seconds at room temperature.
Place the tube back on the magnetic rack.
Remove any residual ethanol and air dry for 30 seconds.
Do not over-dry the pellet.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and add 103 μL of TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0).
Gently flick the tube to ensure that beads are covered in the buffer.
Incubate on a rotator mixer at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Gently flick the tube every 5 minutes to aid resuspension of the pellet.
Pellet the beads on the magnetic rack for at least 10 minutes.
Transfer 100 μL of eluate with a P200 wide bore tip into a 0.2 mL tube.
Prepare the end repair and dA-tailing reaction in a 0.2 mL tube by adding 100 μL of repaired HMW DNA, 14 μL of end repair/dA-tailing buffer, and 7 μL of end repair/dA-tailing mix.
Mix the reaction by flicking gently six times.
Spin down to remove bubbles.
Incubate the reaction at 20 °C for 60 minutes followed by 65 °C for 20 minutes, then hold at 22°C.
Transfer the sample into a new 1.5 mL tube using a P200 wide bore tip.
Resuspend the magnetic beads by pipetting or vortexing.
Add 48 μL of beads (0.4x) to the end repair/dA-tailing reaction and mix gently by flicking the tube six times.
Rotate the tube on a rotator mixer at room temperature at 20 rpm for 30 minutes.

Repeat steps involving spinning down, placing back on magnetic rack, removing residual ethanol and air drying, adding buffer, incubating with resuspension, transferring eluate, preparing reaction, mixing, spinning to remove bubbles, incubating at various temperatures, transferring sample into a new tube, resuspending beads, adding beads to the reaction, and rotating for 30 minutes.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack and add 33 μL of TE buffer (pH 8.0).
Gently flick the tube to ensure beads are covered in the buffer.
Incubate on a rotator mixer at room temperature for 30 min, gently flicking every 5 min.
Pellet the beads on the magnetic rack for at least 10 min.
Transfer 30 μL of eluate into a new 1.5 mL tube using a P200 wide bore tip.
Take extra 1-2 μL to detect concentration using a fluorometer.
Prepare ligation reaction in the 1.5 mL sample tube by adding 30 μL of end-repaired HMW DNA, 20 μL of adapter mix (AMX 1D), and 50 μL of blunt/TA ligation master mix.
Mix gently by flicking the tube 6 times between each sequential addition.
Spin down to remove bubbles.
Incubate reaction at room temperature for 60 min.
Resuspend magnetic beads by pipetting or vortexing.
Add 40 μL beads (0.4x) to the ligation reaction and mix gently by flicking the tube 6 times.
Rotate the tube on a rotator mixer at room temperature at 20 rpm for 30 min.
Repeat step once.
Add 400 μL of adapter bead binding buffer into the tube.
Flick the tube gently 6 times to resuspend beads.
Place the tube back on the magnetic rack to separate beads from buffer and discard supernatant.
Repeat step once.
Spin down the sample at 1,000 x g for 2 seconds at room temperature.
Place the tube back on the magnetic rack.
Remove any residual buffer and air dry for 30 seconds.
Resuspend the pellet in 43 μL of elution buffer.
Incubate on a rotator mixer at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Gently flick the tube every 5 minutes to aid resuspension of the pellet.
Pellet the beads on the magnetic rack for at least 10 minutes.
Transfer 40 μL of eluate with a P200 wide bore tip into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Take the extra 1-2 μL to detect the concentration using a fluorometer.
Thaw the reagents from the transposase kit on ice and pipette to mix.
Thaw fragmentation mix (FRA) and rapid adapter (RAP) on ice and pipette to mix.
Thaw sequencing buffer (SQB), loading beads (LB), flush buffer (FLB), and flush tether (FLT) at room temperature and pipette to mix.
Keep all kit components on ice after thawing.
Take out the enzymes only when needed.
Check the quality and quantity of the HMW DNA.
Pipette out 20 μL of DNA into new 1.5 mL tubes from three different locations in the HMW DNA tube using P200 wide bore tips.
Take 1 μL from the three aliquots to detect the concentration using a fluorometer and the quality using a UV reading.
Check multiple times to confirm the results.
Add 22 μL of HMW DNA into a 0.2 mL tube.
Add 1 μL of 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) with 0.02% Triton X-100 to the tube.
Add 1 μL of fragmentation mix (FRA) to the tube.
Mix by pipetting with a P200 wide bore tip as slowly as possible 6 times, taking care not to introduce bubbles.
Incubate the reaction at 30 °C for 1 min.
Incubate the reaction at 80 °C for 1 min.
Hold the reaction at 4 °C.
Transfer the mix into a new 1.5 mL tube with a P200 wide bore tip.
Add 1 μL of rapid adapter (RAP) to the 1.5 mL sample tube.
Mix by pipetting with a P200 wide bore tip as slowly as possible 6 times, taking care not to introduce bubbles.
Incubate the reaction at RT for 60 min.
Check the nanopore sequencing device software and hardware.
Ensure there is enough storage space on the device.
Insert a new flow cell into the nanopore device.
Select the correct flow cell type for the device.
Start the Check Flow Cells workflow in the software.
Initiate the Start Test button to begin flow cell QC analysis.
Prepare the priming buffer by adding 576 μL of running buffer with fuel mix and 624 μL of nuclease-free water into a 1.5 mL tube for mechanical shearing-based library.
Vortex and spin down the tube to mix the priming buffer thoroughly.
For transposase fragmentation-based library, add 30 μL of flush tether to the tube of flush buffer.
Vortex and spin down the tube containing flush tether and flush buffer to mix the priming buffer thoroughly.
Move the priming port cover clockwise on the flow cell to expose the priming port.
Set a P1000 pipette to 100 μL.
Insert the tip into the priming port.
Draw back a small volume of buffer (less than 30 μL) to remove bubbles from the flow cell.
Stop pipetting once a small amount of yellow fluid enters the tip.
Use a P1000 pipette to load 800 μL of the priming mix into the flow cell via the priming port.
Add 30 μL of the priming mix to cover the top of the priming port first.
Insert the tip into the priming port and slowly add the rest of the priming mix.
Take out the tip when there is about 50 μL left.
Add the rest of the priming mix on the top of the priming port.
Leave the setup to incubate for 5 min.
Prepare the library mix in a 1.5 mL tube containing the library.
For a mechanical shearing-based library, add 35 µL of running buffer with fuel mix (RBF) to 40 µL of the DNA library.
For a transposase fragmentation-based library, add 34 µL of sequencing buffer (SQB) and 16 µL of nuclease-free water to 25 µL of the DNA library.
Open the flow cell sample port cover gently to expose the sample port.
Use a P1000 pipette to add 200 μL of the priming mix through the priming port into the flow cell.
Set a P200 pipette to 80 μL.
Mix the library gently with a wide bore tip by pipetting up and down 6 times just prior to loading.
Load the library mix dropwise through the sample port into the flow cell.
Add each drop only after the previous drop is completely loaded into the port.
Put back the sample port cover gently and make sure the sample port is fully covered.
Move the priming port cover anticlockwise to cover the priming port.
Close the device lid.
Click on the New Experiment workflow.
Type the library name, select the correct kit according to procedures used, and check that the settings are correct (48 h run, real-time base-calling ON).
Click Start Run.
After 10 min, record the flow cell ID and the active nanopore numbers from the run information.
Copy the data to a local computer or a cluster at any time of the sequencing or when the run is complete.
Use Minimap2 to align the sequence data to the reference genome.
Summarize the sequencing performance from the raw sequence data and the alignments by NanoPlot.
